US-12775345-B2.inventionTitle: Displaying a user interface based on activation of a rotatable and depressible input mechanism
US-12775345-B2.abstractHtml: Button functionalities for user interfaces, e.g., for use with a portable multifunction device, are disclosed. Exemplary button functionalities are described for an electronic device with a display, a rotatable and depressible input mechanism, and/or a button. Different device features may be accessed, depending on whether the rotatable and depressible input mechanism or the button is activated, and further depending on whether the activation represents a single press, a double press, or an extended press on the rotatable and depressible input mechanism or the button.

US-12775463-B2.abstractHtml: An apparatus includes a cache memory circuit, and a hierarchal store queue circuit that further includes a primary queue and a secondary queue. The hierarchal store queue circuit may be configured to write incoming store requests to the primary queue in response to the primary queue currently having capacity, and to write incoming store requests to the secondary queue in response to the primary queue currently not having capacity. The hierarchal store queue circuit may be further configured to commit store requests to the cache memory circuit from the primary queue but not from the secondary queue. In response to a determination that the primary queue currently has capacity, the hierarchal store queue circuit may perform a transfer of at least one store request from the secondary queue to the primary queue.

US-12783245-B2.inventionTitle: Training techniques for load value prediction and load address prediction
US-12783245-B2.abstractHtml: Techniques are disclosed relating to load value prediction. In some embodiments, a processor includes load address prediction circuitry and load value prediction circuitry. Training circuitry may train loads in a given entry, and may include a first entry configured to store first predicted load address information and a confidence indication of confidence that the first predicted load address information is correct and a second entry configured to store first predicted load value information and a confidence indication of confidence that the first predicted load value information is correct (note a given entry may be configured for load address prediction or load value prediction at different times). Control circuitry may, in response to an entry in the training circuitry reaching a threshold level of confidence, allocate a corresponding entry in either the load value prediction circuitry or the load address prediction circuitry.

US-20260320992-A1.inventionTitle: IMAGING DEVICE, IMAGING SYSTEM, AND IMAGING DEVICE CONTROL METHOD
US-20260320992-A1.abstractHtml: To suppress performance degradation when sparsity is improved in an imaging device using a neural network. The imaging device includes a predetermined number of output-side neurons and a statistic calculation unit. In this imaging device, each of the output-side neurons generates an output signal on the basis of an input signal from an intermediate layer every time a predetermined unit time elapses. The statistic calculation unit performs, for each output-side neuron, a calculation of a statistic of the output signals generated within a predetermined frame period longer than the unit time.
US-20260320992-A1.claimsHtml:
1. An imaging device comprising a simple detector, wherein the simple detector includes a predetermined number of output-side neurons each configured to generate an output signal on the basis of an input signal from an intermediate layer every time a predetermined unit time elapses; and a statistic calculation unit configured to perform, for each of the output-side neurons, a calculation of a statistic of the output signals generated within a predetermined frame period longer than the unit time.
2. The imaging device according to claim 1, further comprising a function calculation unit configured to output a calculation value obtained by inputting each of the statistics to a predetermined function.
3. The imaging device according to claim 3, further comprising a control unit configured to control a length of the frame period in accordance with a detection result of the simple detector.
4. The imaging device according to claim 3, further comprising a control unit configured to control a threshold value of a neuron in the simple detector in accordance with the detection result of the simple detector.
5. The imaging device according to claim 1, further comprising an image sensor configured to generate image data, wherein the simple detector detects a predetermined detection target from the image data by analysis.
6. The imaging device according to claim 5, further comprising: a detail detector configured to detect a predetermined detection target from the image data by a more detailed analysis than the simple detector; an evaluator configured to generate an evaluation value from the image data by an analysis different from the analysis by the detail detector; and a rule selection unit configured to select a rule for controlling operations of the detail detector and the evaluator, on the basis of a detection result of the simple detector.
7. The imaging device according to claim 6, wherein the simple detector and the detail detector are disposed in a neural network circuit.
8. The imaging device according to claim 6, wherein the simple detector, the detail detector, and the evaluator are disposed in a neural network circuit.
9. The imaging device according to claim 6, further comprising an input control unit configured to control an operation of the image sensor on the basis of the detection result of the simple detector.

US-20260328905-A1.abstractHtml: A machine learning (ML) model may be trained using a self-supervised approach. Training sensor data may be provided to the ML model, and the ML model may estimate one or more object properties based on the training sensor data. Reconstructed sensor data may be generated based at least on the estimated object properties. The reconstructed sensor data may be of a same data type as the training sensor data. One or more parameters of the ML model may be updated based at least on a comparison between the training sensor data and the reconstructed sensor data. A machine may obtain sensor data using one or more sensors. The machine may determine one or more properties corresponding to an object based at least on the ML model processing the sensor data. US-20260333439-A1.abstractHtml: Wireless IEEE 802.11 communication mechanisms are described for a member STA of a R-TWT SP to gain TXOP channel access before the R-TWT SP, which does not need to end before the start time of the R-TWT SP. On trigger based R-TWT SP, the TXOP time is shared to overlap the R-TWT SP; allowing the AP to behave as the TXOP holder for the frame exchange of latency sensitive traffic during the R-TWT SP. Thus, the R-TWT scheduling AP and member STAs of a R-TWT SP can contend for the channel together before the scheduled start time of the R-TWT SP. When one of these STAs gains channel access, it can reserve a TXOP until the scheduled end time of the R-TWT SP, which may extend beyond the normal TXOP limit.

An example can provide top caps for charging pucks that have multiple layers. A top cap can include a top compliant layer that deform to contact the electronic device over an increased area.
